# VergeIO Provider

The provider is used to interact with resources and data sources supported by VergeOS.

Use the navigation on the left to read about the available resources and data sources this provider can use.

## Support
VergeIO welcomes pull requests and responds to issues on a best-effort basis. VergeIO maintains public GitHub repositories for initiatives that help customers integrate the VergeIO platform with other third-party products. Support for these initiatives is handled directly via the GitHub repository. Issues and enhancement requests can be submitted in the Issues tab of each repository. Search for and review existing open issues before submitting a new issue.

## Example Usage

Username and password:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    vergeio = {
      source  = "verge-io/vergeio"
      version = "~> 3.0"
    }
  }
}

provider "vergeio" {
  host     = "vergeos.example.com"
  username = "my_user"
  password = "my_password"
  insecure = false
}
```

API key. When `api_key` is set, it is used instead of `username` and `password`.

```terraform
provider "vergeio" {
  host    = "vergeos.example.com"
  api_key = var.vergeos_api_key
}
```

Every argument is optional. The provider reads the matching environment variable when an argument is omitted. A value in the provider block wins.

```terraform
# VERGEOS_HOST
# VERGEOS_API_KEY, or VERGEOS_USERNAME and VERGEOS_PASSWORD
# VERGEOS_INSECURE, or VERGEOS_VERIFY_SSL=false
# VERGEOS_TIMEOUT (seconds)
provider "vergeio" {}
```

A tenant is created on the parent system. Resources inside that tenant use a second Terraform configuration, because the tenant address is not known until the parent configuration has been applied and the tenant is online. See the [tenants guide](guides/tenants.html).

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Arguments

- `host` - (String, Optional) VergeOS hostname or IP address, with or without an `https://` prefix. Environment variable: `VERGEOS_HOST`.
- `username` - (String, Optional) Username used with `password`. Environment variable: `VERGEOS_USERNAME`. Required when `api_key` is unset.
- `password` - (String, Sensitive, Optional) Password used with `username`. Environment variable: `VERGEOS_PASSWORD`. Required when `api_key` is unset.
- `api_key` - (String, Sensitive, Optional) API key sent as a bearer token. Environment variable: `VERGEOS_API_KEY`. Used instead of `username` and `password` when both forms of authentication are set.
- `insecure` - (Boolean, Optional) Skip TLS certificate verification for systems with self-signed certificates. Defaults to `false`. Environment variable: `VERGEOS_INSECURE`. `VERGEOS_VERIFY_SSL=false` means the same thing as `insecure = true`. When both environment variables are set and `insecure` is omitted, they must agree.
- `timeout` - (Number, Optional) HTTP request timeout in seconds. Defaults to `60`. Environment variable: `VERGEOS_TIMEOUT`.

The provider fails during configuration, before the first API request, when `host` is missing or when neither an API key nor both a username and password are available. That error names each missing value.

Configurations written for 2.x need the [v3.0 upgrade guide](guides/version-3-upgrade.html) before changing the version constraint to `~> 3.0`. Until then, pin `~> 2.7`.
